results.content: President Trump’s approval rating dipped again this week, following a downward trend in support for the president amid the ongoing Iran war and mounting affordability concerns ahead of November’s midterms. The latest survey from The Economist/YouGov, published Monday, found 33 percent of respondents said they approved of how Trump has handled his job as president. Support for the president was split largely along partisan lines, with 79 percent of GOP respondents and only 4 percent of Democratic respondents approving of Trump’s job performance, according to the poll. results.content: President Donald Trump has broken his own record for the lowest approval rating recorded by The Economist/YouGov, with just 33 percent of Americans now saying they approve of the way he is handling his job as president. What To Know The significance of the latest result is ultimately less about one number than about the trajectory. Trump Hits New Lows Among Key Blocs Trump’s approval is also reaching new lows across several key voting blocs. Trump has a new net approval low among white Americans too, with a 39 percent approval in the new poll compared to 57 percent disapproval. results.content: Shifting Support Among Key Voters The latest Economist/YouGov Poll released on August 11 shows the lowest net approval ratings Trump has received among women (-36), white Americans (-19) and college graduates (-42). Economic Concerns Heading Into the Midterms Americans continue identifying the economy as the most important issue facing the country—one that will remain top of mind as voters head to the ballot box come November.
